knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Dust falls, so working from the top down means dust lands only on surfaces still to be cleaned.
Loading the cloth controls where the product goes and keeps spray off floors and fittings.
Equipment that is left dirty or wet creates a slip hazard and can spread soil to the next job, so it is cleaned, dried and stored first.

practicalCriteria: Dusts vertical surfaces from the top down, refolding or changing the duster when loaded, observed by the assessor.
Applies the solution to the cloth and wipes without spray reaching the floor or fittings, observed by the assessor.
Checks and stores the equipment before leaving the area, recorded on the checklist.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. Practical competence: assessor sign-off against each practical criterion, observed on site or in a simulated setting. A knowledge-check pass does not verify practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation sheet for dusting and damp wiping
Completed task checklist with the solution batch recorded
stopWorkCriteria: Solution is sprayed onto a floor or onto a surface not covered by the task
Wet equipment is left in a walkway
A product is made up stronger than the label allows
